security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI configures only PMP/Smepmp or only MPT (but not both) when enforcing physical memory isolation for supervisor domains during domain context switches. The updated spec now requires both mechanisms independently (SR_SUD_001 for PMP/Smepmp, SR_SUD_002 for MPT), where previously only one was needed (old SR_SUD_001 used 'or'). An OpenSBI implementation that relies on MPT alone without also programming PMP/Smepmp entries to isolate supervisor domains violates SR_SUD_001. Conversely, an implementation that configures only PMP/Smepmp without an MPT for page-granularity domain isolation violates SR_SUD_002.
security_spec.summary: SR_SUD_001/002 split requires both PMP/Smepmp AND MPT for domain isolation; OpenSBI must configure both during domain context switches, not just one

findings.finding: SR_SUD_001 (PMP/Smepmp): Domain context switch correctly reconfigures PMP by unconfiguring the old domain's PMP entries and configuring the new domain's PMP entries. For smepmp, firmware PMP entries (M-only code/data regions) are preserved across the switch. An SFENCE.VMA + HFENCE.GVMA fence is issued at the end of smepmp_configure/oldpmp_configure to flush cached PMP translations. This satisfies the PMP/Smepmp requirement for supervisor domain isolation.

findings.finding: SR_SUD_002 (MPT): No MPT/MMPT programming occurs during domain context switches. Only PMP entries are reconfigured via sbi_hart_protection_unconfigure/configure(). MPT-based page-granularity domain isolation is never established, leaving supervisor domains protected only by coarse-grain PMP regions. The MPT component (CSR definitions, hardware detection, entry programming) is entirely absent from the codebase.

SR_SUD_002 (MPT): The hart protection framework uses a single-winner design — sbi_hart_protection_best() returns the highest-rated mechanism from a ranked list, and configure/unconfigure dispatch only to that single winner. Even if an MPT backend were registered, it would either replace PMP (if higher rated) or be ignored (if lower rated). The framework cannot configure two protection backends simultaneously, making independent PMP+MPT enforcement structurally impossible.

SR_SUD_002 (MPT): No SBI_HART_EXT_MPT or SBI_HART_EXT_MMPT entry exists in the hart extension enum. The codebase enumerates 21 extensions (SMAIA, SMEPMP, SMSTATEEN, SSCOFPMF, SSTC, ZICNTR, ZIHPM, ZKR, SMCNTRPMF, XANDESPMU, ZICBOZ, ZICBOM, SVPBMT, SDTRIG, SMCSRIND, SMCDELEG, SSCSRIND, SSCCFG, SVADE, SVADU, SMNPM, ZICFILP, ZICFISS, SSDBLTRP, SMCTR, SSCTR, SSQOSID, SSSTATEEN) but none for MPT/MMPT. Hardware MPT support cannot be detected or enumerated.

SR_SUD_002 (MPT): mseccfg CSR (0x747) is defined with only MML, MMWP, RLB, USEED, SSEED bit macros — all Smepmp-related. No MPT/MMPT/SDID-related CSR definitions or mseccfg field macros exist. The CSR encoding foundation needed to program MPT entries is entirely absent.

findings.finding: SR_SUD_001 (PMP/Smepmp): Correctly detects Smepmp vs legacy PMP and registers the appropriate protection backend (epmp_protection rating 200, or pmp_protection rating 100). The higher-rated smepmp backend includes map_range/unmap_range for dynamic shared-memory access via reserved PMP entry 0, satisfying the PMP requirement for domain isolation.

spec_citations.excerpt: Since all fields defined in mseccfg as part of this extension are locked when set (MMWP/MML) or locked when cleared (RLB), software can't poll them for determining the presence of Smepmp. It is expected that BootROM will set mseccfg.MMWP and/or mseccfg.MML during early boot.

findings.finding: SR_SUD_002 (MPT): Cold boot path calls only sbi_hart_protection_configure() which dispatches to PMP/Smepmp. The same applies to init_warm_startup (line 473) and init_warm_resume (line 494). Across the entire HART lifecycle — cold boot, warm boot, and suspend-resume — MPT-based fine-grain domain isolation is never established. Only coarse-grain PMP protects domains at init time.

SR_SUD_001 (PMP/Smepmp): Full Smepmp configure correctly: (1) sets RLB to bypass lock enforcement during programming, (2) disables reserved entry 0, (3) programs M-only regions first with firmware region tracking via bitmap, (4) enables MML to enforce Smepmp encoding, (5) programs shared and SU-only regions, (6) disables unused entries, (7) calls sbi_hart_pmp_fence() for SFENCE.VMA+HFENCE.GVMA. Firmware regions are preserved across domain switches via fw_smepmp_ids bitmap.
